topic: Density-free attainment of the KBRW pointwise-CATE benchmark under a fixed positive two-sided covariate-density band. In the i.i.d. observational Holder model with strict overlap, bounded outcomes, alpha-smooth propensity, beta-smooth control regression and gamma-smooth continuous CATE, treat all smoothness indices and radii as known class inputs and construct one total local R-estimator using no density estimate or density smoothness. Let (h_n^*,k_n^*) be the lexicographically smallest optimizer of h^gamma+(h/k^(1/d))^(alpha+beta)+[1/(n h^d){1+k/(n h^d)}]^(1/2), N_n^*=n(h_n^*)^d, G_n={k_n^* log^3(n)<=N_n^*}, and P_n=G_n^c. Prove uniformly on compact smoothness sets that mean-absolute risk is at most the KBRW benchmark with no logarithmic loss: use a same-sample Mobius-stabilized empirical-Gram local HOIF on G_n and a finite-order multiresolution close-pair correction on P_n, with total bounded fallbacks. The P_n theorem must strictly extend the banked low-smoothness 0<beta<alpha<=1 region to a derived nonempty open subset outside it. Do not assume or claim a density-induced slowdown, do not use KBRW's support-hole fuzzy-hypothesis family as a positive-band converse, and do not treat local Gram singularity as an all-estimator lower bound. Estimator algebra, correction order and proof mechanics are outputs of the solve.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one everywhere-defined density-free local R-estimator attain the optimizer-defined KBRW pointwise-CATE benchmark without logarithmic loss across both the locally rank-feasible and rank-stressed regimes under only a fixed two-sided covariate-density band?

source_refs.claim: KBRW derives the pointwise-CATE benchmark, but its attaining construction uses conditions involving the local covariate law and leaves the density's role unresolved.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Same-sample stabilized empirical HOIFs remove density estimation for global bilinear functionals, but do not address localized pointwise CATE or random local occupancy.
source_refs.author: Na Liu, Chang Li, Yujia Gu, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: A two-regime random-design functional estimator combines close-pair and HOIF mechanisms, but targets homoskedastic variance rather than CATE.
source_refs.author: Edgar Dobriban, Rajarshi Mukherjee, James M. Robins, Zixiao Wang

source_refs.excerpt: extension beyond the close-pair region, and logarithm removal remain open.
Log removal outside R_pair also remains unresolved, and alpha<beta lies outside the currently defined R_low.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked density-free construction reaches the KBRW rate only on a proper close-pair wedge and uses a logarithmically inflated rank-capped fallback elsewhere. Meanwhile, the component literatures use incompatible normalizations and exceptional events: stabilized HOIF controls a global empirical Gram when k/n is small, close-pair methods control random cell occupancy, and KBRW localizes at effective size n h^d. A resolution must prove that same-sample Gram failures, empty cells, collision terms, bounded fallbacks, and the deterministic branch transition all contribute no more than the uninflated optimizer value, uniformly over compact smoothness sets and without estimating the design density.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A single measurable bounded estimator, switching only according to G_n versus P_n and defined on every sample, with a compact-uniform mean-absolute-risk bound by a constant times the exact infimum of the KBRW three-term objective.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the pointwise Hölder model, regression-versus-functional motivation, elbow phenomenon, and exact benchmark the unified estimator must attain.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pointwise CATE combines local regression with nonlinear nuisance adjustment -> low nuisance smoothness creates a functional-estimation branch -> positive-band density-free implementations face complementary occupancy regimes -> stitch stabilized-HOIF and close-pair branches into one benchmark-rate estimator

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the localized R-projection and quadratic-HOIF decomposition that produces the target approximation, projected nuisance-product, linear-variance, and degenerate-variance terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This decomposition defines the precise risk envelope and optimizer that both branches must reproduce.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt same-sample inverse-Gram stabilization, Möbius cancellation, truncated Neumann expansion, and graph-counting variance bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It addresses the empirical-Gram dependence obstruction on the rank-feasible branch, with n h^d replacing the global sample size.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its totalized sparse-cell close-pair construction and two-regime HOIF/close-pair risk accounting.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest existing example of joining the two mechanisms, although the causal residual algebra and density-band proof remain new.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a same-sample Möbius-stabilized empirical-Gram local HOIF attain the KBRW local R-risk bound whenever k log³(n) is at most n h^d?

source_refs.claim: KBRW's localized higher-order R-learner supplies the benchmark decomposition but retains conditions involving estimation of the local covariate distribution.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Möbius cancellation and graph counting stabilize same-sample empirical-HOIF Gram inversion for global bilinear functionals, not localized CATE.
source_refs.author: Na Liu, Chang Li, Yujia Gu, Lin Liu

source_refs.claim: Empirical HOIF replaces a density-dependent projection by an inverse sample Gram matrix, but uses an independent Gram sample and a below-rank restriction.
source_refs.author: Lin Liu, Rajarshi Mukherjee, Whitney K. Newey, James M. Robins

source_refs.excerpt: combine same-sample Möbius-stabilized Gram corrections at distinct propensity and outcome-regression resolutions
State the uniform Gram-conditioning lemma for the chosen partition series as an intermediate target

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proposal named the same-sample Möbius program but proved only an independent-fold, rank-capped construction. Localization changes the global stabilized-HOIF argument because the effective Gram sample is random and of order n h^d, the basis and leverage depend on h, and the same weighted observations occur in both inverse-Gram factors and higher-order kernels. The first missing proof step is a localized Möbius moment expansion whose collision counting, conditional spectral event, truncation remainder, and bounded bad-Gram fallback are uniform in the optimizer and sharp enough to avoid a union-bound logarithm.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit same-sample local-HOIF estimator with separate finite-sample bounds for projection bias, Möbius remainder, collision variance, Gram-failure contribution, and total risk matching the KBRW objective throughout k log³(n) ≤ n h^d.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames the destination as optimal pointwise CATE estimation and supplies the local R-object whose density-dependent projection must be replaced.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Pointwise CATE requires localization -> rough nuisances require a growing higher-order projection -> density-based projection control is not available under a bare density band -> stabilize the same-sample empirical local Gram in the optimizer's rank-feasible region

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the stabilized inverse-Gram polynomial, Möbius inversion of index coincidences, Neumann remainder control, and graph-counting variance proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired local correction has the same random bilinear inverse-Gram structure, with effective sample size n h^d and kernel-weighted occupancy.

method_exemplars.technique: Use empirical projection geometry to eliminate density smoothness and bound projection bias through the sample Gram rather than a density estimate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the foundational density-free empirical-HOIF construction whose splitting and rank restrictions the localized stabilization must sharpen.

method_exemplars.technique: Insert the empirical-Gram correction into the localized R-score while preserving its three benchmark terms.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those are exactly the risk terms the statement-level resolution must bound.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a finite-order multiresolution close-pair correction attain the KBRW pointwise-CATE benchmark in the sparse-local regime and on a derived nonempty open smoothness region strictly extending beyond 0<β<α≤1?

source_refs.claim: KBRW identifies the functional-estimation branch of the pointwise-CATE benchmark but does not supply a density-free sparse-window close-pair implementation.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: A two-scale eligible-close-pair construction handles low-regularity random-design variance estimation, but does not derive the causal residual identity or CATE smoothness frontier.
source_refs.author: Edgar Dobriban, Rajarshi Mukherjee, James M. Robins, Zixiao Wang

source_refs.claim: A local-polynomial pairwise-difference U-statistic attains random-design minimax rates for pointwise variance estimation, providing a close noncausal analogue.
source_refs.author: Yandi Shen, Chao Gao, Daniela Witten, Fang Han

source_refs.excerpt: extend the close-pair upper bound off the alpha<=1, beta<alpha subregion (higher-order pair differences for alpha>1)
characterize the corresponding band-only frontier for the opposite ordering alpha<beta
midpoint localization and sufficiently close covariate pairs turn treatment and outcome differences into a local R-norma

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked pair estimator uses a first close-pair difference and midpoint symmetry, then relies on β<α≤1 to dominate asymmetric increment terms. Variance-estimation close-pair identities automatically cancel a common regression mean, whereas CATE requires a bilinear treatment-residual/outcome-residual correction with two unequally smooth nuisances, strict-overlap weights, and a local target projection. The first proof step that must change is the conditional pair identity: a finite multiscale signed combination of pairs or tuples must impose enough vanishing moments to cancel the lower Taylor terms separately, retain a positive local R-Gram, and produce Hoeffding variances compatible with the optimizer.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit finite correction order q(α,β,γ,d), a bounded multiresolution close-pair local R-statistic, and a KBRW-rate risk bound on k log³(n)>n h^d over a stated nonempty open smoothness set intersecting {β≥α} or {α>1}.

writing_exemplar.why: Its smoothness phase diagram makes the destination region and benchmark transparent without implying that the noncausal close-pair donors posed this CATE problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The KBRW benchmark varies with two nuisance smoothness indices -> density-free first differences attain it only in an asymmetric low-order wedge -> higher smoothness or reversed ordering breaks midpoint cancellation -> derive the correction order and enlarged attainable region

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt sparse-cell pair selection, local-polynomial trend removal, and two-resolution cancellation, together with occupancy-based risk control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its mechanism is designed for poorly populated empirical-projection regimes matching the sparse-local obstruction, though its target is constant variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize its local pairwise-difference U-statistic and Hoeffding decomposition to signed multiresolution causal residual kernels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems use random-design close-pair geometry to estimate a localized functional whose rate mixes target and nuisance smoothness.

method_exemplars.technique: Choose a finite higher-order estimating equation so successive nuisance products replace first-order bias, then control all resulting degenerate Hoeffding components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested correction order must be determined by the same smoothness-versus-degenerate-variance calculation.

open_problems.open_problem: Does a density-free benchmark-rate pointwise-CATE estimator admit honest studentization at x₀ across the KBRW elbow, including regimes where a degenerate HOIF or sparse close-pair component is first-order?

source_refs.claim: KBRW establishes mean-error minimax rates but does not provide a pointwise limit law or confidence interval across its low-smoothness elbow.
source_refs.author: Edward H. Kennedy, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, James M. Robins, Larry Wasserman

source_refs.claim: Doubly robust CATE confidence bands cover a first-order local-smoothing regime, not the low-smoothness minimax HOIF regime.
source_refs.author: Sokbae Lee, Ryo Okui, Yoon-Jae Whang

source_refs.claim: Uniform coverage-error expansions exist for ordinary local-polynomial regression but not for CATE estimators with first-order degenerate HOIF or close-pair components.
source_refs.author: Sebastian Calonico, Matias D. Cattaneo, Max H. Farrell

source_refs.claim: Higher-order influence-function theory develops interval procedures for nonlinear functionals, but not localized pointwise CATE under random window occupancy.
source_refs.author: James M. Robins, Lingling Li, Eric Tchetgen Tchetgen, Aad van der Vaart

open_problems.why_unsolved: In the regression-like region the linear local-polynomial term may support Gaussian studentization, while at and below the elbow a degenerate U-statistic or selected close-pair component can be first-order and may have a different limit. Same-sample Gram stabilization adds dependent random coefficients absent from standard local-polynomial inference. The missing proof step is a regime-uniform Hájek/Hoeffding projection result with feasible variance estimation and negligible stabilization and fallback events; existing CATE bands assume first-order asymptotics, while ordinary local-polynomial coverage theory omits the causal higher-order component.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A feasible studentized statistic with a uniform Gaussian limit and honest pointwise coverage on an explicit smoothness region, together with a regime-stated non-Gaussian limit or impossibility result wherever uniform Gaussian studentization fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly motivates uncertainty quantification for heterogeneous effects and separates causal nuisance adjustment from low-dimensional local smoothing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: CATE estimates guide heterogeneous decisions -> point estimates do not quantify local uncertainty -> doubly robust smoothing enables bands in first-order regimes -> extend honest inference to minimax HOIF and close-pair regimes

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the uniform Edgeworth expansion, explicit smoothing-bias accounting, robust bias correction, and studentized coverage analysis for local polynomials.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies inference machinery for the local target component; the resolution must add causal nuisance and higher-order degenerate terms.

method_exemplars.technique: Use higher-order influence-function interval construction and Hoeffding-projection analysis in non-root-n functional regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest limit-theory template when the higher-order correction rather than the linear local-regression term governs uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over doubly robust pseudo-outcome construction followed by local smoothing and Gaussian approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly targets CATE inference and provides the first-order comparison case for the low-smoothness extension.

literature_map:
Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2203.00837) derive the sharp pointwise-CATE rate and a localized quadratic-HOIF R-learner, but their upper theorem retains conditions on estimating the local covariate law and leaves the density's role unresolved.
Kennedy (2023, Electronic Journal of Statistics, arXiv:2004.14497) supplies preceding local-polynomial doubly robust bounds and the oracle-rate motivation, but not the final low-smoothness minimax construction.
Nie and Wager (2021, Biometrika, arXiv:1712.04912) formulate the R-loss and quasi-oracle property; its first-order nuisance product is the baseline improved by higher-order correction.
Gao and Han (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2002.06471) give a different minimax HTE theory using covariate geometry and nearest-neighbor matching, showing that random-design geometry can replace routine density estimation in related settings.
Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2008, arXiv:0805.3040) introduce rate-optimal higher-order influence-function point and interval estimators as higher-order U-statistics.
Van der Vaart, Tchetgen Tchetgen, Robins, and Li (2009, Metrika, DOI:10.1007/s00184-008-0214-3) develop quadratic von Mises and U-statistic calculus closely related to KBRW's correction.
Robins, Li, Mukherjee, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart (2017, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1512.02174) show how finite HOIF order trades successive nuisance-error products against degenerate U-statistic variance.
Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017, arXiv:1705.07577) replace density estimation by an inverse empirical Gram matrix, eliminating density smoothness while using an independent Gram sample and a below-rank condition.
Liu, Mukherjee, Robins, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2021, JMLR, arXiv:1608.01364) develop multiresolution second-order U-statistics across parametric and nonparametric functional regimes.
Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026, arXiv:2607.04743) stabilize same-sample HOIFs using Möbius cancellation, Neumann expansion, graph counting, and Efron-Stein bounds; their theorem is global rather than pointwise CATE.
Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1902.10822) attain random-design pointwise variance-function rates with a local-polynomial pairwise-difference U-statistic.
Dobriban, Mukherjee, Robins, and Wang (2026, arXiv:2609.08783) combine a two-scale eligible-close-pair construction for low regularity with an HOIF branch for random-design variance estimation; searches found no CATE transplant.
Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017, Journal of Applied Econometrics, arXiv:1601.02801) provide doubly robust CATE confidence bands in a first-order smoothing regime, leaving low-smoothness HOIF inference uncovered.
Calonico, Cattaneo, and Farrell (2022, Bernoulli, arXiv:1808.01398) provide uniform local-polynomial Edgeworth and coverage-error theory that could serve as an inference donor after higher-order terms are incorporated.
prior_proposal_map:
Downgraded stat_cate_density_bottleneck/v1 was the highest-signal source; its README, proto_core, writeup, and open obligations isolate logarithm removal, opposite nuisance ordering, and the unexecuted same-sample Möbius handle.
Its reviews/angle0_v1.json yielded strengthening paths for a reusable uniform Gram-conditioning lemma and a second nuisance ordering.
Its reviews/review_general.json supplied the prescriptive higher-order-pair-difference extension beyond α≤1 and β<α.
Downgraded stat_dp_cate_minimax_v1/holder_central_dp was inspected for its warning that KBRW matching is established only on a density/Gram-stable submodel.
Downgraded stat_cate_local_overlap_nuisance_frontier/v1 and its angle reviews were inspected; their propensity-zero and full-support converse questions do not fit the present strict-overlap upper-bound target.
Downgraded stat_sa_cate_pointwise/v1 was inspected; its point-target well-posedness issue is already repaired by the present continuous Hölder-CATE model.
Downgraded eid_dml_orthogonality_frontier/v1 rejected angles were inspected; their local-HOIF-order ideas are less direct than the risk-attainment opportunities retained here.
No rejected-angle archive exists in stat_cate_density_bottleneck/v1; its abandoned programs are retained as named handles in proto_core.json and writeup.tex.
